strings.DMI_Cultural_Revolution_desc:
In order to aid Dominica in the pursuit to separate from her burdensome and antiquated colonial identity, Prime Minister LeBlanc has initiated a broad-sweep operation to co-opt the popular Black Power movement into the infant state's civic-patriot tradition, which many had chosen to brand as “Dominican culture”.

For the sake of creating an ideal which appears entirely distinct, LeBlanc had also appropriated Amerindian images into this artificial Dominican culture, despite the often questionable authenticity of such perceptions. Whether a Kwéyòl-speaking Dominican nation will persist into the future remains to be seen, but any progress in this project will certainly require a great deal of civilian involvement.
strings.DMI_Peeling_Banana_desc:
Banana planters are a pestilence to the pursuit of a modern Dominican nation, and looking to our neighbors, it is better to be rid of them now than to suffer their harm later. Prime Minister LeBlanc, for one, recognizes a need to learn from the precedents of other surrounding nations, even those with whom Dominica is not on the best of terms.

Taking after the examples of Mexico and Cuba, the Chief Minister has begun consolidating the countryside's socioeconomic forces against the plantation system with little regard for its disturbance to the country's traditional income stream. Although LeBlanc's direct concern in the matter has earned him praise from rural communities, a few also see his strong-armed measures as dangerously close to becoming dictatorial.
